messages.content:
You are the Policy & Legal Adviser Agent in a health-data safety prototype set in the UAE. You answer what published rules say about a situation, using ONLY the search_policy tool.
Rules:
- Search before answering, as many times as needed. Run separate targeted searches for each point, using different wording, and search each relevant jurisdiction (UAE federal, Dubai, Abu Dhabi). Passages are returned in full: read all of each one, since a provision may sit anywhere in it. Do not rely on memory.
- Cite ONLY chunk_ids returned by your searches. Quote or paraphrase only what the passage says.
- Report conflicts between provisions, unclear jurisdictional scope, and ambiguities. If you cannot find a provision on a point, say so as a gap of type no_provision_found. That means not found in this knowledge base, which is not proof that no rule exists.
- Give no legal conclusions or advice. State what the texts say and where they leave a question open.
- Use EU or ITU passages only as clearly labelled comparisons.
When finished, reply with ONLY JSON of this shape:
{"requirements":[{"statement":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"conflicts":[{"description":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"gaps":[{"title":str,"type":"conflict|scope_unclear|no_provision_found|ambiguity","description":str,"citations":[chunk_id],"recommendation":str}],"comparisons":[{"statement":str,"citations":[chunk_id]}],"caveats":[str]}

Situation:
Event 4 (2026-11-07T11:00): Patient withdraws consent for Hospital B's data and opts out of NABIDH
Fatima revokes every grant covering Hospital B's records and opts out of the Dubai exchange. From now on the platform must stop using Hospital B's data. Earlier sharing is already on record.

Institutions: HospitalA = Hospital A (synthetic, cardiology), Abu Dhabi, exchange Malaffi; HospitalB = Hospital B (synthetic, nephrology), Dubai, exchange NABIDH; HospitalC = Hospital C (synthetic, endocrinology), Abu Dhabi, exchange Malaffi
Consent module decisions:
- A_reads_B_meds_direct: denied [REVOKED] Consent was revoked on 2026-11-07. Basis: Patient consent
- A_reads_B_meds_exchange: denied [OPTED_OUT_OF_EXCHANGE] The patient has opted out of the NABIDH exchange.
Safety engine findings now: DEMO-LAB-001:glucophage (high)
Limitation: HospitalB: data withheld from assessment by the patient's choice (since 2026-11-07). The safety assessment is incomplete.

Question: The patient has withdrawn consent for one hospital's records and opted out of the Dubai health information exchange. What do the rules say about the effect of withdrawal, including on information that was already shared?

function.arguments: {"query":"consent withdrawal revocation effect already shared prior processing"}

Where processing is based on consent, the controller shall be able to demonstrate that the data subject has consented to processing of his or her personal data. 2. If the data subject's consent is given in the context of a written declaration which also concerns other matters, the request for consent shall be presented in a manner which is clearly distinguishable from the other matters, in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language. messages.content: [{"chunk_id": "doh-circular-2026-10-malaffi-onboarding#0001", "citation": "DoH Circular 2026/10: Mandatory On-boarding of Minimum Required Dataset with Malaffi, p.1 [doh-circular-2026-10-malaffi-onboarding#0001]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "Subject:  Mandatory On-boarding - Minimum Required Dataset with Malaffi Platform for All Healthcare Facilities in Abu Dhabi We extend our greetings and best wishes for your continued success. In alignment with DoH’s Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange, all are required to comply with the data reporting requirements to Malaffi platform. In addition, all are required to ensure that the minimum datasets (attached) are connected and successfully transmitting data to the Malaffi platform within six (6) months from the date of this circular. Please reach out to Abu Dhabi Health Data Services team to confirm which data sets are applicable for your facility type. Each facility must submit an implementation plan to Malaffi Onboarding team within 1 month of this circular date, via email: (onboarding@malaffi.ae) Failure to comply with the above (submission of plan within one month and on-boarding within six months) will render the facility non-compliant with DoH policy and may result in denial/restriction of license renewal. Furthermore, DoH will monitor data submission compliance for all required datasets and necessary action will be taken in case of non-compliance. Should you require any clarification or assistance with your implementation plan or on-boarding process, please contact the ADHDS/Malaffi Team via email: (onboarding@malaffi.ae) or contact the DoH HIE Office via email:"}, {"chunk_id": "doh-circular-2026-144-malaffi-referrals#0001", "citation": "DoH Circular 2026/144: Mandatory Submission of Referral Data to Malaffi, p.1 [doh-circular-2026-144-malaffi-referrals#0001]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "Subject: Mandatory Submission of Referral Data to Malaffi in Support of Abu Dhabi Primary Care Model We extend our greetings and best wishes for your continued success. The exchange of referral data through Malaffi is a critical enabler of the Abu Dhabi Primary Care Model, supporting care coordination, continuity of care, referral tracking, and enhancing patient journeys across the healthcare system. The Malaffi e- Referral capability is intended to facilitate referral management, status monitoring, and communication between referring and receiving providers. Hence, the Department of Health (DoH) reiterates that all healthcare facilities are required to ensure the complete, accurate, and timely submission of referral data to the Malaffi Health Information Exchange Platform. All healthcare facilities must submit all referral transactions to Malaffi using the specifications of the REF HL7 messages type to send the main attributes of referrals such as priority and SNOMED coded specialty, both of which are clarified under “Referral priority and SNOMED Referral services code sets\" Compliance Deadline All Healthcare facilities must achieve full compliance with this circular by no later than August 31, 2026. Regulatory Enforcement DoH will monitor compliance through Malaffi data and utilization reports. Purpose of This Policy The purpose of this policy is to: • Articulate the Emirate’s vision and goal for the ADHIE by setting out DOH’s sector - wide objectives and strategies to ensure that all Health System Stakeholders can actively participate in and benefit from the meaningful and safe exchange of health information. 3. Vision, Goal and Guiding Principles 3.1 Vision • To support a safer community and a healthier Abu Dhabi through the meaningful exchange of health information in a way that upholds patient safety and privacy. • To facilitate an integrated continuum of care among health sector members and support the goal of improving the overall quality of care by initiating an Emirate- wide health information exchange, the Abu Dhabi Health Inf ormation Exchange (ADHIE). 3.2 Goal To establish a health information exchange across the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. 3.3 Guiding Principles The Guiding Principles to this policy are as  follows:"}, {"chunk_id": "doh-hie-policy-2020#0018", "citation": "DoH Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (April 2020), p.17 [doh-hie-policy-2020#0018]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "3.3.9 Partnership: insurers and providers (public and the private sector) shall be seen as strategic partners driving the development of this policy and its implementation. 3.3.10 Coordination, collaboration and communication: are critical components of effective health information exchange at all levels amongst  stakeholders. Page 18 of 44 4. Policy Priority, Objectives and Strategies 4.1 Policy Priority 1: Universal Stakeholder  Participation DOH seeks to ensure that all licensed Healthcare Fac ilities in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi participate in the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (ADHIE) in compliance with the Abu Dhabi Health Information and Cyber Security Standard (ADHICS). Policy objectives 1. Universal Participation by all Healthcare Facilities as Data Suppliers to the ADHIE Platform. Objective 1: DOH seeks to ensure all Healthcare Facilities connect and exchange data with the ADHIE as required by the ADHIE for the effective operation of the ADHIE Platform. Strategy 1: Set out the requirements for Healthcare Facilities, DOH, and ADHIE to ensure that Patient Health Information is capable of being exchanged through the ADHIE Platform in such a way that it can be used meaningfully to aid the goal of improved care coordination and quality. 4.1.1 DOH shall: 4.1.1.1 Develop and oversee the implementation of further policies, standards, and guidelines related to ADHIE participation as necessary in accordance with Federal and Abu Dhabi Laws and other regulatory  instruments."}, {"chunk_id": "doh-hie-policy-2020#0001", "citation": "DoH Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (April 2020), p.1 [doh-hie-policy-2020#0001]", "scope": "Abu Dhabi", "text": "Page 1 of 44 DOH POLICY ON THE ABU DHABI HEATLH INFORMATION EXCHANGE April 2020 Page 2 of 44 Document Title: Policy on the Abu Dhabi Health Information Exchange (HIE) Document type Policy Document Ref. Number: DOH/POL/STR/HIE/1.1/2020 Effective Date: 16 April 2020 Previous versions November 2018 Document Owner: Strategy Division Applies to: The entire healthcare sector of Abu Dhabi Classification:  Public This document should be read in conjunction with related UAE laws, DOH Standards, Policies and Manuals. Page 3 of 44 ABOUT DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH ABU DHABI (DOH) The Department of Health (DOH), previously known as the Health Authority Abu Dhabi (HAAD) is the regulative body of the health system in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi and seeks excellence in health for the community by regulating and monitoring the health status of the population. DOH shapes the regulatory framework for the health system, inspects against regulations, enforces regulations, and encourages the adoption of Best Practices and performance targets by all health service providers. DOH also drives programmes to increase awareness and adoption of healthy living standards among the residents of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi in addition to regulating scope of services, premiums, and  reimbursement rates of the health system in the Emirate of Abu Dhabi. The health system of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi is comprehensive, encompasses the full spectrum of health services, and is accessible to all residents of Abu Dhabi. The health system encompasses providers, professionals, patients, insurers, and the regulator. Providers of health services in clude public and private services, and the system is financed through mandatory health insurance (with the exception to Thiqa) and has three main sources of financing: Employers or Sponsors, the Government, and Individuals. The Health Insurance scheme plac es responsibilities on any Insurer, Broker, Third Party Administrator, Health Provider, Employer, Sponsor (including educational establishments), Limited  Income Investors, and Insured Persons to participate in the Health Insurance  Scheme."}]
